item.title: Exclusive: US military had close call after using AI for false intelligence report, sources say
item.description:
# Exclusive: US military had close call after using AI for false intelligence report, sources say It was only just before the planned operation that officials dug deeper into the report put together by a special operations command analyst and found it had been generated with the help of artificial intelligence (AI) — and that a chatbot the analyst had used inaccurately identified the material the ship was carrying.
In January, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth released his agency’s “Artificial Intelligence Acceleration Strategy” in a bid to speed up the military’s use of AI.

item.title: Trump to create ‘AI Force’ to monitor technology as fears over out-of-control agents grow
item.description:
# Trump to create ‘AI Force’ to monitor technology as fears over out-of-control agents grow [Donald Trump](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump) on Saturday said he would appoint an [artificial intelligence](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/artificialintelligenceai) czar and create an “AI Force” to help monitor the technology, though he gave almost no details about either plan.
The latest, he wrote, is “the decimation, or destruction, of AI, commonly known as Artificial Intelligence”, and vowed that his administration “will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry”.
The post came [after an earlier missive](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117298413844042212) in which he questioned the term “artificial intelligence” – coined by American computer scientist John McCarthy in 1955 and defined as the capability of computer systems or algorithms to imitate intelligent human behavior – to describe the accelerating data-processing revolution now under way.

The “mostly retired” professor at the University of Colorado Boulder was the first woman to earn a Ph.D. in the field of artificial intelligence at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland in the 1980s and spent her career working primarily in language processing and machine translation.

item.title: How Is Artificial Intelligence Insured?
item.description:
# The Insurability of Artificial Intelligence ResearchPublished Sep 16, 2026
- [Email](mailto:?subject=RAND%3A%20The%20Insurability%20of%20Artificial%20Intelligence&body=From%20RAND%0A%0AThe%20Insurability%20of%20Artificial%20Intelligence%0A%0AA%20mismatch%20exists%20between%20rapid%20enterprise%20adoption%20of%20artificial%20intelligence%20%28AI%29%20and%20the%20market%20for%20insuring%20it.%20This%20report%20examines%20AI%20incidents%2C%20lawsuits%2C%20laws%2C%20and%20insurance%20filings%20to%20assess%20coverage%20responses%20and%20accumulation%20risks.%0A%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.rand.org%2Fpubs%2Fresearch_reports%2FRRA5130-1.html)
Businesses increasingly embed artificial intelligence (AI) in operations, products, and services, creating both new opportunities and new forms of risk. Firms are deploying AI in customer service, employment screening, coding, fraud detection, and autonomous systems. At the same time, AI-related harms are already emerging, including incorrect or misleading outputs, deepfakes, privacy violations, intellectual property disputes, fraud, product defects, and discriminatory decisions.
